title: Orsen and the Safehouse
premise: Ines Winterbourne, a sleepless interpreter for a fragile peace delegation, is the only person who notices that a diplomatic flight has been erased from every record while still airborne. Pulled into an off-the-books investigation by a disgraced air-safety investigator named Orsen, she uncovers a conspiracy inside the delegation's own security apparatus: a second attack, scheduled to destroy the peace talks and be written off as mechanical failure. As Ines and Orsen race through safehouses, forged manifests, and betrayals by people she once trusted, Ines must choose between her duty of neutrality and the justice no court will deliver. The book ends with Ines exposing the plot at the signing ceremony itself—sacrificing her career and nearly her life—and walking away from the institution she served, alive but permanently changed.
about_author: Silas Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent years around border crossings, briefings, and the paperwork of things governments prefer forgotten. He writes thrillers about ordinary professionals trapped inside machinery designed to make them complicit.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Silence
chapters.summary: POV Ines. At a tense pre-summit briefing in Geneva, Ines translates a security chief's assurances while privately doubting them; she hasn't slept through the night since 'the incident' months ago. A colleague warns her to stay invisible. Emotional beat: exhaustion masked as professionalism, and the first flicker that something in the room is wrong.

chapters.title: Flight 4471
chapters.summary: POV Ines. A delegation support flight departs at dusk with documents Ines helped translate. Mid-evening, its tracking blip vanishes; by morning, the flight number appears in no database, manifest, or memory of the tower staff. Her inquiries are gently deflected. Emotional beat: gaslit vertigo—the horror of being the only witness to a fact everyone denies.

chapters.title: A Man Who Collects Wrecks
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Following a name scrawled on a discarded maintenance log, Ines finds Orsen Kade, a dismissed crash investigator living above a marine salvage yard. He listens when no one else will, and shows her how erasures leave seams. Emotional beat: wary recognition between two people who refuse to unsee things.

chapters.title: Seams in the Record
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Orsen walks Ines through the forensic traces: a fuel purchase with no destination, a crew roster pulled two hours before departure. Someone didn't just hide a flight—they rebuilt the day around its absence. Emotional beat: dread hardening into purpose as coincidence dies.

chapters.title: The Safehouse
chapters.summary: POV Ines. After a surveillance team photographs her outside Orsen's yard, he moves her to a decommissioned border station—his old safehouse. They work through the night mapping who benefited from the vanished flight. Emotional beat: intimacy born of danger; the first honest conversation either has had in years.

chapters.title: What the Delegation Buried
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. The erased flight carried evidence: black-box duplicates proving a prior 'accident' was sabotage, meant to derail the talks. Whoever destroyed it is protecting the saboteur. Emotional beat: the case stops being about one plane and becomes about a pattern of engineered tragedy.

chapters.title: Old Loyalties
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Ines is summoned by Deputy Chief Halvard Renner, her mentor, who offers protection in exchange for dropping her questions. He mentions her sister by name—a threat dressed as concern. Emotional beat: love against duty; the institution that raised her revealing its teeth.

chapters.title: Ghost Manifest
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Orsen bribes a freight clerk and recovers a partial cargo list: among diplomatic crates, a mislabeled container routed to the summit venue's service tunnels. Weight and dimensions suggest ordnance. Emotional beat: cold clarity—the next attack already has a delivery date.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Cross-referencing schedules, they fix the attack window: nine days out, timed to look like a gas main failure during the signing gala. Ines drafts an anonymous report to the oversight board. Emotional beat: hope curdling as she realizes the board's chair dines with Renner.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Their only outside contact, a young archivist named Pell, is found drowned—an 'accident.' Orsen understands they were allowed to move so someone could watch. Emotional beat: grief and guilt; the cost of the truth measured in someone else's life.

chapters.title: Countermove
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Renner announces an internal inquiry—into Ines, for mishandling classified material. Her credentials are suspended; her apartment is searched. She becomes officially invisible, exactly as she'd always tried to be. Emotional beat: bitter irony; invisibility as weapon turned against her.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Key
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Among Pell's effects, smuggled to them by his sister, is an access key to the delegation's sealed evidence vault. Inside the vault's index: the original sabotage report, signed off by three names—one is Renner's. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by despair at how high it goes.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: POV Ines. With six days left, they plan to copy the vault file, but the safehouse is compromised; they relocate through freight yards at night. In a stolen hour, Ines admits why she can't sleep: she interpreted the transcript of the first 'accident' and ignored what it implied. Emotional beat: confession; her guilt reframed as complicity she must now undo.

chapters.title: Inside the Vault
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Using Pell's key during a shift change, Orsen copies the sabotage report while Ines runs interference as a translator for an unrelated inspection. They barely clear the building before the alarm protocol locks down. Emotional beat: adrenaline and trust—the pair functioning as one organism.

chapters.title: Renner's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Renner corners Ines alone: join him, help shape the aftermath, and her sister stays safe; the attack will proceed regardless, and history will thank whoever writes it. He speaks of peace as arithmetic—lives weighed against stability. Emotional beat: power's corruption laid bare as seduction rather than menace.

chapters.title: The Second Container
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Physical recon of the venue's service tunnels confirms the container's position beneath the east hall—directly under where delegations will sign. Orsen maps a way to expose it publicly: force an independent inspection before the gala. Emotional beat: grim resolve; the plan requires going loud, which means going hunted.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Yard
chapters.summary: POV Ines. The salvage-yard ally who fed Orsen information sells them out; armed men burn the safehouse. Ines and Orsen escape separately, losing the copied files to fire. All that remains is what's in their heads. Emotional beat: loss stripped to essentials—each other, the timeline, and the truth memorized.

chapters.title: Two Days
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. With files gone, their last route is human testimony: a guilt-wracked logistics officer willing to speak if given immunity. Orsen trades his own remaining credibility—contacting a journalist he once despised—to guarantee coverage. Emotional beat: sacrifice of self-protection; justice outside the law demands burning your own standing.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Hiding in a chapel annex near the summit, Ines sleeps for the first time in months—two hours, dreamless—then wakes certain of what she must do: not leak quietly, but stand up mid-ceremony and interpret the sabotage report aloud, in every delegate's language. Emotional beat: peace found not in safety but in decision.

chapters.title: The Signing
chapters.summary: POV Ines. During the gala, as pens touch paper, Ines takes the floor and begins translating the buried report. Chaos erupts; Renner orders her seized; delegates demand answers. The journalist's live feed forces an emergency evacuation of the east hall. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into voice—the invisible woman making herself unmistakable.

chapters.title: What the Tunnels Held
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Evacuated minutes before detonation, the east hall collapses into the tunnel blast; the 'gas accident' happens without its intended victims. Orsen delivers the logistics officer's sworn testimony to international observers as Renner is detained trying to flee. Emotional beat: catharsis with ash on it—justice delivered, imperfectly, in daylight.

chapters.title: After the Silence
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Weeks later, testifying before an independent tribunal, Ines declines reinstatement. She visits Pell's grave, then meets Orsen at the salvage yard, where nothing is decided and everything is possible. She sleeps through the night. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—love chosen over duty, and a life rebuilt outside the machinery.
